context_summary: The paper introduces AutoPCM, an automated LLM-based approach to identify circular design potentials in automotive electronics. It uses LLMs to analyze manufacturing documents, generate product architecture decompositions, and evaluate circular strategies. The approach is validated on two automotive case studies.
exclusion_facts: No human evaluations were found in the paper.

title: CarvGPT: a multi-agent collaborative framework for cultural translation and digital innovation in traditional craft design
scope_note: 全文逐页规则筛查＋高相关证据页语义清点；证据链仅保留PDF原句定位，未使用旧表内容。
context_summary: The paper proposes CarvGPT, a multi-agent framework for cultural translation and digital innovation in traditional craft design. It integrates requirement analysis, cultural parsing, and visual generation to support designers in translating cultural connotations into design concepts.

title: Large Language Model Agent as a Mechanical Designer

context_summary: This paper proposes a framework using a pretrained Large Language Model (LLM) coupled with a Finite Element Method (FEM) module to autonomously generate, evaluate, and refine structural designs. The LLM operates without domain-specific fine-tuning, relying on general reasoning to iteratively propose candidate structures, interpret FEM-derived results, and implement informed modifications grounded in structural mechanics.

context_summary: This paper introduces a multimodal-conditioned fashion image editing framework using latent diffusion models. The approach incorporates text, body pose, garment sketches, and fabric textures to guide the generation process. The study extends existing fashion datasets with multimodal annotations and evaluates the realism and coherence of generated images using quantitative metrics and human evaluations.

title: Exploring Optimal Combinations: The Impact of Sequential Multimodal Inspirational Stimuli in Design Concepts on Creativity
scope_note: 全文逐页规则筛查＋高相关证据页语义清点；证据链仅保留PDF原句定位，未使用旧表内容。
context_summary: This study investigates how the sequence of multimodal inspirational stimuli (text, images, virtual models) affects designers' creativity during the design conception phase. A platform called InspireMe was developed to present these stimuli in various sequences, and 36 novice designers participated in the study. The results show that the sequence of stimuli significantly influences creativity, with different impacts on sub-attributes of creativity. The study proposes a Creativity Demand-Matching Inspirational Interaction Strategy (CDI) and a 3C Framework for creativity stimulation platforms.
